The state of the nation. Water shocked again by the worssning floods each rainy season, Filipinos could care less about the opening of the 20th Congress today. 

Not much has been done after the disaster that was Ondoy in 2009 which submerged Metro Manila in water. Except perhaps for one of the most affected, which is Marikina. 

Through its own efforts of adding box culverts the the necessity of adding to the NCR water supply, which resulted in the rehabilitation of the Wawa Dam, Marikina didn't experience flooding, except for the riverside communities, at the onslaught of the habagat. 

The same couldn't be said for others parts of NCR+, including Cavite, Laguna and Bulacan, which all went under water again. 

Coming on the heels of the midterm election loss by the administration, a high-level revamp was initiated but didn't amount to much in the end. 

It must have been the opening salvo in an integrated PR effort which has seen the president becomes more visible. But it's not well-orchestrated because the optics comes off a forced - hinog sa pilit kumbaga. 

The US trip and the audience with the great white father was supposed to bring the bacon home for the SONA, so to speak. 

This fizzled out as well as Trump used the event to his advantage. The first from ASEAN but so what? Not too many are making a beeline to the US to pay homage to the Donald nowadays given his tariffs. 

ASEAN relations with the US is cordial but it's obviois also that the choice has been made. There is more room to grow with China. The other ASEAN heads of state see no compelling reason to go to the US. They would rather see Xi in China or as what Xi did instead, which was to go on an ASEAN swing earlier this year. 

The 1% reduction in tariff is minuscule compared to what we have given the Uncle Sam in the EDCA sites and the stationing of missile systems pointed at China. 

Use of leverage should've resulted in at least a tariff of say, 15%, or even 10% as a true friend, partner and ally. 

To top it off, the supreme court ruled against the impeachment of the vice-president. The justices must be sending a message to the administration. There are still two pending cases with the high court and an adverse ruling on both won't bode well for the administration since it concerns the transfer of Philhealth funds and the 2025 national budget. 

The pressen situation begs the question, kaya pa ba Pilipinas? We all know where the bulk of the flood control project funds go. Yet, those who claim to be para sa bayan are more concerned with the impeachment of the vice-president which goes to show that it's not about the country and its long suffering citizens but vested interests. 

Hangga't hindi lumulubog ang mga tirahan nila wala silang pakialam dun sa mga lumulubog ang mga bahay tuwing panahon ng habagat. 

This is no different from the matuwid na daan at kung walang corrupt, walang mahirap period in our history. It's all the same cast of characters. 

But if you accept that this is the new normal and can live with it, what can be done? 

The operative phrase is kung hindi tayo kikilos, sino? 
https://t.co/iATtupUmqt
